title: Expecting a parcel? That "missed delivery" text may be a scam
description:
Got a "we missed your delivery" text? Don't tap the link.

Fake parcel delivery texts claim a missed delivery or an address problem. The link opens a look-alike site that asks for your personal details or a small "redelivery fee". Massachusetts' Office of Consumer Affairs repeated this warning for the holiday season.

In the US, people reported losing $470 million to text scams in 2024, and fake package delivery was the most commonly reported type (US FTC, April 16, 2025).

In the UK, Action Fraud warns the small payment can be step one: days later, a spoofed "bank" call or text tells you to move your money to a "secure" account that the criminals control.

Analyst note: the small fee is the bait. What they really want is your card details.

Do this tonight:
1. Don't tap the link in the text.
2. Track the parcel in the carrier's own app or website, or on the shop's site where you ordered.
3. Forward the text to 7726, the spam reporting number in the US and UK. If you already paid, call your bank right away.

Sources
- US FTC press release (Apr 16, 2025): https://www.ftc.gov/node/88093
- Massachusetts Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation, Outsmart Scammers This Holiday Season: https://www.mass.gov/news/outsmart-scammers-this-holiday-season
- Action Fraud (UK), fake DPD messages alert: https://www.actionfraud.police.uk/alert/fake-dpd-messages-lead-to-over-200000-in-losses-since-june

Narration uses an AI voice (ElevenLabs). Research, script and fact-check by Securidge.

#cybersecurity #scam #smishing
